records.title: Ordered practice funnel
records.subtitle: Recorded live-model answer on synthetic data
records.review_note: One real-provider smoke, not a benchmark. AI-assisted review of this sample only; not a human review. Verified each displayed value and qualitative definition against actual funnel evidence and retrieved contract. No significance, causal, rollout, or equal-count comparability claim.

report.question: Compare the ordered practice funnel.
report.summary: The ordered practice funnel shows a decrease in the signup-to-practice start rate from before to after, dropping from 84.6 % to 70.4167 %. The practice completion rate within seven days also decreased, from 56.2167 % before to 30.5 % after. Conditional completion rate, the rate of completion given practice start, declined from 66.45 % before to 43.3136 % after. The funnel analysis counts unique users and matches start and completion session identifiers in timestamp order within seven days of signup, as defined in the ordered practice funnel contract.

retrieval.title: Ordered practice funnel
retrieval.text: The funnel is signup to practice start to practice completion within seven days. Count unique users and match start/completion session identifiers in timestamp order. Report both signup-to-step and conditional completion rates.

retrieval.title: Supported analytical scope
retrieval.text: Only activation, ordered funnel and onboarding_valid/onboarding_srm experiments are defined. Segment by acquisition channel or signup device. Engagement, revenue, retention and arbitrary custom metrics are not defined; clarify or abstain.

retrieval.title: Effect uncertainty
retrieval.text: Report treatment minus control in percentage points with a 95% Newcombe score interval based on Wilson intervals. An interval crossing zero is inconclusive, not proof of no effect. Statistical significance alone does not justify shipping.

evidence.sql:
WITH starts AS (
  SELECT e.user_id, e.practice_session_id, MIN(e.event_at) AS started_at
  FROM events e JOIN users u USING(user_id)
  WHERE e.event_type='practice_start' AND e.practice_session_id <> ''
    AND e.event_at >= u.signup_at AND e.event_at < u.signup_at + INTERVAL 7 DAY
  GROUP BY e.user_id, e.practice_session_id
), completions AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT e.user_id FROM events e
  JOIN starts s ON e.user_id=s.user_id AND e.practice_session_id=s.practice_session_id
  JOIN users u ON e.user_id=u.user_id
  WHERE e.event_type='practice_complete' AND e.event_at >= s.started_at
    AND e.event_at < u.signup_at + INTERVAL 7 DAY
), cohort AS (
  SELECT u.*, CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM starts s WHERE s.user_id=u.user_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS started,
    CASE WHEN c.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS completed
  FROM users u LEFT JOIN completions c USING(user_id)
  WHERE u.signup_at >= CAST(? AS TIMESTAMP) AND u.signup_at < CAST(? AS TIMESTAMP)
    AND u.signup_at + INTERVAL 7 DAY <= CAST(? AS TIMESTAMP)
) SELECT COUNT(*) denominator, COALESCE(SUM(started),0) started, COALESCE(SUM(completed),0) numerator FROM cohort

records.title: Retail sales · live model
records.subtitle: Recorded development-only live-model answer on public retail data
records.review_note: Development-only recorded sample, not a benchmark. Automatic numeric/citation checks: passed. Human semantic review status: required; whole-task outcome: unscored.

report.question: Which countries contributed to the sales change?
report.summary: The United Kingdom was the largest contributor to the sales increase between the two months. United Kingdom: Sales change contribution: 386,371.2 GBP. Several countries including Japan, EIRE, and Norway also contributed positively to the sales change. Japan: Sales change contribution: 6,512.04 GBP; EIRE: Sales change contribution: 6,420.51 GBP; Norway: Sales change contribution: 2,840.27 GBP. Some countries such as the Netherlands, Australia, and Singapore contributed negatively to the sales change. Netherlands: Sales change contribution: -14,834.64 GBP; Australia: Sales change contribution: -9,907.81 GBP; Singapore: Sales change contribution: -7,067.32 GBP. The total sales change is the sum of all country contributions, confirming an accounting decomposition rather than causal attribution. Sales change: 354,517.03 GBP.

retrieval.title: Country contribution to sales change
retrieval.text: Subtract October 2011 gross positive sales from November 2011 for each country. Country contributions sum to the total change. Countries absent in one month contribute zero in that month. This is an accounting decomposition, not causal attribution.

retrieval.title: Source and quality boundaries
retrieval.text: UCI Online Retail by Daqing Chen (2015), DOI 10.24432/C5BW33, CC BY 4.0. Public historical UK retailer transactions from December 2010 to December 2011. Exact duplicate rows are retained and counted because no source line ID proves which repeated lines are erroneous. Only complete October and November 2011 are compared.

retrieval.title: Gross positive sales in GBP
retrieval.text: Sum Quantity times UnitPrice for invoice lines with positive quantity and price, excluding cancellation invoices starting C. This is gross positive sales, not net revenue, profit, or causal uplift. Missing customer identifiers do not exclude a valid sales line.

evidence.sql:
SELECT month, SUM(gross_sales_gbp), SUM(orders), SUM(lines), SUM(units)
FROM retail WHERE month IN (?, ?) GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

SELECT country,
SUM(CASE WHEN month=? THEN gross_sales_gbp ELSE 0 END) AS before_gbp,
SUM(CASE WHEN month=? THEN gross_sales_gbp ELSE 0 END) AS after_gbp
FROM retail WHERE month IN (?, ?) GROUP BY country ORDER BY country
